_doc: Requirements catalogue for action-receipt.md. `anchor` is text copied verbatim from the spec; conformance/trace.py --check verifies it still occurs there. Edit this file directly, then run conformance/trace.py --render.

requirements.text: Perform the steps in order and stop at the first failure.
requirements.anchor: The verifier MUST perform the steps below **in order** and MUST stop at the first failure.

requirements.text: Check §5.3 in its stated order: integer `version`, `version == 1`, member set and grammar, outcome, status, bindings array, bindings.
requirements.anchor: Reject with the code shown, checking in this order:

requirements.text: Never raise, and never return ERROR, because of anything in the receipt or the x402 objects.
requirements.anchor: It MUST NOT raise, and MUST NOT return `ERROR`, because of anything in the receipt or in the x402 objects.
requirements.note: properties P6 and P7 on both implementations: ERROR only when the configuration is outside the contract; the generator mutates header member types and text (non-string alg, NaN, huge integers, deep nesting) and x402 values of every type; the cited vectors pin the reviewer B-2 inputs

requirements.text: A verifier fault is ERROR, never reported as a rejection (and the reverse).
requirements.anchor: `ERROR` says nothing about the receipt and MUST NOT be reported as a rejection.

requirements.text: Return ERROR for configuration outside the contract (mode, clock, maximum age, paid resource URL), whatever the receipt.
requirements.anchor: A verifier given configuration outside this contract returns `ERROR`.

requirements.text: Never substitute a default or nearest valid value for configuration it cannot read.
requirements.anchor: It MUST NOT substitute a default or the nearest valid value: a mode it does not recognize is not `archival`, and a maximum age it cannot read is not 3600.

requirements.text: The clock is an integer number of Unix seconds in [-(2^53 - 1), 2^53 - 1] (read by value; a boolean is not one): both ends are valid, one past either end is ERROR.
requirements.anchor: an integer number of Unix seconds

requirements.text: The paid resource URL is absent or a string.
requirements.anchor: not supplied or `null`, meaning the verifier did not pay; or a string

requirements.text: Reject a receipt that is not a JWS-format object with a string signature of three base64url segments.
requirements.anchor: Reject with `invalid_payload` unless the receipt is an object with `format == "jws"`

requirements.text: Accept only the one base64url spelling of a byte string.
requirements.anchor: re-encoding the decoded bytes MUST reproduce the string

requirements.text: Reject a compact string longer than 65536 characters.
requirements.anchor: `signature` is a string of at most 65536 characters

requirements.text: Ignore any other member of the receipt object.
requirements.anchor: Any other member of the receipt object is ignored and is not covered by the signature.

requirements.text: Reject a header with a byte-order mark, in another encoding, with a repeated member, with NaN, or out of order.
requirements.anchor: A header with a byte-order mark, in another encoding, with a repeated member, with `NaN`, or with members out of order fails here.

requirements.text: The header has one spelling: its bytes are the JCS form of the header object.
requirements.anchor: The header bytes are the RFC 8785 serialization of that object, so a header has one spelling

requirements.text: The header passes the full canonical-bytes test of §5.2, value domain included, before `typ` is read.
requirements.anchor: the first decodes to bytes `H` that pass the test of §5.2

requirements.text: Reject unless `typ` is the string `x402-action-receipt+jws`.
requirements.anchor: Reject with `invalid_actionreceipt_typ` unless the header's `typ` is

requirements.text: Never verify an action receipt as a base receipt or the reverse.
requirements.anchor: A verifier MUST NOT verify an action receipt as a base receipt or the reverse

requirements.text: Reject unless `alg` is ES256, ES256K or EdDSA.
requirements.anchor: Reject with `invalid_actionreceipt_alg` unless `alg` is

requirements.text: An `alg` of any other type is rejected with the alg code, never an ERROR.
requirements.anchor: A value of any other type is rejected here.

requirements.text: Reject unless the header has exactly `alg`, `kid`, `typ` and `kid` is a string.
requirements.anchor: Reject with `invalid_payload` unless the header has exactly the members

requirements.text: Reject payload bytes that are not valid UTF-8 JSON.
requirements.anchor: `B` is valid UTF-8 and parses as JSON (RFC 8259)

requirements.text: Reject a payload outside the value domain: integers outside [-(2^53 - 1), 2^53 - 1], unpaired surrogates, nesting deeper than 8; a payload at those bounds passes this step.
requirements.anchor: the parsed value lies in the value domain of §4.6

requirements.text: Reject payload bytes that are not exactly the JCS form of their value.
requirements.anchor: `JCS(parsed value) == B`, byte for byte

requirements.text: Check canonical bytes before any typing, and let any canonical JSON value through to the schema step.
requirements.anchor: This step comes **before** any typing

requirements.text: Reject unless the payload is an object with an integer `version` member.
requirements.anchor: `invalid_payload` unless the value is an object that has a `version` member whose value is an integer.

requirements.text: Reject any `version` other than 1, before the member set is checked.
requirements.anchor: `invalid_actionreceipt_version` unless `version == 1`

requirements.text: Reject a payload without exactly the listed members, a member of the wrong type, or one outside its grammar.
requirements.anchor: `invalid_payload` unless the object has exactly the members of §4.1

requirements.text: A network identifier has a 3 to 32 character namespace and a 1 to 32 character reference; non-CAIP-2 identifiers such as `cloudflare:402` are valid.
requirements.anchor: The `network` grammar is the CAIP-2 shape with a longer namespace.

requirements.text: `payer` may be empty on any network; on eip155 a non-empty `payer` is lowercase hex.
requirements.anchor: `payer` when `network` begins `eip155:` and it is non-empty

requirements.text: The EVM rules apply only when `network` begins `eip155:`; a network that merely looks similar gets none of them.
requirements.anchor: `payTo` when `network` begins `eip155:`

requirements.text: Reject a signed member that is out of grammar; never repair it (EVM identifiers must already be lowercase).
requirements.anchor: A signed member that does not match its grammar is rejected; it is never repaired.

requirements.text: Compare strings as exact code-point sequences; apply no normalization to signed members.
requirements.anchor: No Unicode normalization, case folding, percent-decoding or URL normalization is applied to any signed member.

requirements.text: Accept each listed `outcome` and reject any other.
requirements.anchor: `invalid_actionreceipt_outcome` unless `action.outcome` is a listed value

requirements.text: Accept each listed `settlementStatus` and reject any other.
requirements.anchor: `invalid_actionreceipt_status` unless `settlementStatus` is a listed value

requirements.text: Reject with `invalid_payload` when `bindings` is not an array.
requirements.anchor: `invalid_payload` unless `bindings` is an array.

requirements.text: `chargedAmount` is `""`, `0` or a decimal integer of at most 78 digits with no leading zero; any other value, or one that is not a string, is rejected.
requirements.anchor: a decimal integer of at most 78 digits, no leading zero

requirements.text: Reject a `bindings` array that breaks the entry shape, grammar, order, uniqueness or count; accept one at every bound.
requirements.anchor: `invalid_actionreceipt_binding` unless `bindings` satisfies §4.5

requirements.text: The `action-receipt:` namespace is closed: only the two types of §4.5.2, each with its value form.
requirements.anchor: every entry whose `type` begins `action-receipt:` is one of the two types of §4.5.2 with a `value` of that type's form

requirements.text: Do not reject a receipt for an unrecognized binding type; report it as not evaluated.
requirements.anchor: A verifier MUST NOT reject a receipt because it does not recognize a binding type.

requirements.text: No binding status changes the verdict.
requirements.anchor: No binding status changes the verdict.

requirements.text: Evaluate `action-receipt:advertised-info` when the advertised `info` is held in the value domain: digest, then `scope` and `actionType` equality.
requirements.anchor: `matched` iff the digest is equal and, for each of `scope` and `actionType` that is a member of `info`, its value is a string equal to the receipt's `action` member

requirements.text: `action-receipt:reversal-transaction` is never evaluated offline.
requirements.anchor: Never offline. A verifier that resolves it on the rail reports the result itself

requirements.text: Report `checks.advertisement`: not_evaluated without held info, absent without the binding, else the binding's status.
requirements.anchor: A per-entry status cannot show an entry that is missing, so the report also carries `checks.advertisement`:

requirements.text: Reject with the signer code when the source answered and `kid` is not among the keys it lists for the resource.
requirements.anchor: the source answered, and `kid` is not among the keys it lists for the resource. Reject with `invalid_actionreceipt_signer`.

requirements.text: When the authorization source gives no answer, reject as unresolved, never as a signer finding.
requirements.anchor: The verifier MUST NOT report this as `invalid_actionreceipt_signer`: failing to reach a source is not a finding against the signer.

requirements.text: In the key fixture an authorization entry that is not an array of strings authorizes nothing.
requirements.anchor: a value that is not an array of strings authorizes nothing

requirements.text: Treat both anchors as scoped to the resource.
requirements.anchor: Both anchors are scoped to the resource.

requirements.text: Never take the location of authorization data from `kid`; a `did:web` kid on another host is not authorized under (a).
requirements.anchor: It MUST NOT take it from `kid`: a `did:web` `kid` whose host is not the host of `resourceUrl` is not authorized under (a) unless a registry the verifier trusts says so.

requirements.text: In archival mode, judge authorization as of `issuedAt`.
requirements.anchor: In `archival` mode the question is whether the key was authorized when the receipt was issued

requirements.text: Report an authorized key that cannot be obtained, or is not a usable public key, as unresolved, not as a bad signature.
requirements.anchor: reject with `invalid_actionreceipt_key_unresolved`

requirements.text: Only a public key is a usable key: a private key, a certificate, or a PEM with anything around it is not.
requirements.anchor: A private key, a certificate, or a public

requirements.text: Verify the signature over the first two segments under the resolved key.
requirements.anchor: Reject with `invalid_actionreceipt_signature` unless the signature verifies over

requirements.text: Require the key's type and curve to match `alg`.
requirements.anchor: the key's type and curve match `alg`

requirements.text: Require 64-byte low-s ECDSA signatures.
requirements.anchor: ECDSA signatures are the 64-byte `r || s` form of RFC 7518 §3.4 and MUST be low-`s`

requirements.text: Reject unless `success` is the boolean true and the response provides an identifier.
requirements.anchor: Reject with `invalid_transaction_state` unless the `SettlementResponse` has `success == true`

requirements.text: The receipt's `transaction` equals the response's when the response has one.
requirements.anchor: If the response has a `transaction`, the receipt's `transaction` equals it.

requirements.text: The receipt carries no `transaction` the response does not have.
requirements.anchor: If the response has none, the receipt's `transaction` is `""`.

requirements.text: The receipt's `settlementRef` equals the response's settlement reference when it has one.
requirements.anchor: If the response has a settlement reference, the receipt's `settlementRef` equals it.

requirements.text: The receipt carries no `settlementRef` the response does not have.
requirements.anchor: If it has none, the receipt's `settlementRef` is `""`.

requirements.text: The receipt's `chargedAmount` equals the response's charged amount when it has one.
requirements.anchor: the receipt's `chargedAmount` equals it.

requirements.text: The receipt carries no `chargedAmount` the response does not have.
requirements.anchor: If it has none, the receipt's `chargedAmount` is `""`.

requirements.text: The response's charged amount is `extra.chargedAmount` when present, else `amount` when present (§4.6), whatever the scheme.
requirements.anchor: `extra.chargedAmount`, else `amount`, each when present

requirements.text: The charged amount is not normalized: a response amount that is out of grammar equals no receipt's.
requirements.anchor: Nothing is normalized: an amount spelled `010` in the response is not `10`

requirements.text: Compare `network` when the response's is a network identifier; otherwise record that it was not compared.
requirements.anchor: If the response's `network` is a network identifier (§4.6), the receipt's `network` equals it.

requirements.text: Compare `payer` when the response has one; otherwise record that it was not compared.
requirements.anchor: If the response has a `payer`, the receipt's `payer` equals it.

requirements.text: Lowercase the response's `transaction` and `payer` on `eip155` networks before comparing.
requirements.anchor: it lowercases the response's `transaction` and `payer`

requirements.text: Normalize nothing else: a settlement reference and every value off eip155 are compared exactly.
requirements.anchor: Nothing else is normalized.

requirements.text: A value read from an unsigned object is present only as a non-empty string of well-formed Unicode; anything else is absent.
requirements.anchor: when it is a non-empty string of well-formed Unicode. Anything else is absent:

requirements.text: When the accepted requirements are held, `requirementsDigest` must equal their digest.
requirements.anchor: `requirementsDigest` equals the digest computed per §4.4

requirements.text: Canonicalize with members sorted by UTF-16 code units, not code points.
requirements.anchor: members sorted by UTF-16 code units

requirements.text: The accepted `network` must equal the receipt's.
requirements.anchor: `accepted.network` equals the receipt's `network`

requirements.text: The accepted `payTo`, lowercased on `eip155`, must equal the receipt's.
requirements.anchor: `accepted.payTo`, lowercased on `eip155` networks, equals the receipt's `payTo`

requirements.text: When requirements are not held, or are not a JSON object in the value domain, record that they were not evaluated.
requirements.anchor: records `requirements: not_evaluated` and `payTo: not_compared`

requirements.text: Judge numbers by value, not spelling: `60.0` is the integer 60.
requirements.anchor: The test is on the number's value, not its spelling

requirements.text: Reject a receipt dated more than 60 seconds in the future, in both modes.
requirements.anchor: In both modes, reject with `invalid_actionreceipt_freshness` if `age < -60`.

requirements.text: In session mode, reject a receipt older than the maximum age; the maximum age may be 0 or as large as 2^53 - 1.
requirements.anchor: In `session` mode, also reject if `age > maxAge`.

requirements.text: With no maximum age configured, the maximum age is 3600 seconds.
requirements.anchor: The default `maxAge` is 3600 seconds.

requirements.text: In archival mode, report age and do not reject on it.
requirements.anchor: In `archival` mode age is not a reason to reject.

requirements.text: Return the report with every PASS.
requirements.anchor: A verifier MUST make at least this available:
requirements.note: every positive's full report is declared by hand in the suite (EXPECT_REPORT over a default written from §5.12) and compared member by member; run_vectors.py compares the full published report for any adapter

requirements.text: `receiptRef` is the hash of the payload bytes and covers neither header nor signature.
requirements.anchor: so the same statement signed under two keys has one `receiptRef`
requirements.note: sameReceiptRef and distinctReceiptRef relations in the manifest; the suite checks each positive's receiptRef against the payload segment's hash; fuzz property P1 on both implementations

requirements.text: Two statements that differ only in `receiptId` are two receipts.
requirements.anchor: It exists so that two statements which share every other member are still two receipts.

requirements.text: Every signed member is covered: changing any one changes `receiptRef`, and the members the context constrains are rejected.
requirements.anchor: Each signed member of a positive is changed once and re-signed.
requirements.note: the 17-member mutation matrix, with a guard that fails a mutation that changes nothing

requirements.text: A verifier that made the payment rejects a receipt whose `resourceUrl` is not, as an exact string, the URL it paid for.
requirements.anchor: `invalid_actionreceipt_resource_mismatch` unless the receipt's `resourceUrl` equals, as an exact string, the resource URL it paid for

requirements.text: A non-requesting verifier says that its inputs were recorded copies.
requirements.anchor: It MUST say so when it reports a result

requirements.text: When resolving on the rail, confirm the chain, success, asset, amount, payer and recipient.
requirements.anchor: A verifier that does so SHOULD confirm that the node serves the chain named by `network`

requirements.text: Do not assume the transaction's submitter is the payee.
requirements.anchor: It SHOULD NOT assume the transaction's submitter is the payee

requirements.text: Pass the conformance suite before reporting a canonicalization rejection against an issuer.
requirements.anchor: A verifier SHOULD pass the conformance suite (§7) before reporting one against an issuer.

requirements.text: Retain the key and authorization evidence relied on, with the resolution time.
requirements.anchor: Verifiers that retain receipts SHOULD retain the key and the authorization evidence they relied on

requirements.text: Advertise the extension in `PaymentRequired`.
requirements.anchor: A resource server that will issue receipts SHOULD advertise the extension

requirements.text: Carry the advertised `actionType` and `scope` in the receipt.
requirements.anchor: the receipt it later issues MUST carry the same values

requirements.text: Commit the advertisement with the `advertised-info` binding; the client's echo is not what is committed.
requirements.anchor: the server commits the advertisement with the `action-receipt:advertised-info` binding

requirements.text: May emit both a base receipt and an action receipt.
requirements.anchor: A server MAY emit both a base receipt and an action receipt for one settlement.

requirements.text: When both are emitted, `network` and `resourceUrl` are equal and `payer` and `transaction` name the same account and transaction.
requirements.anchor: When it does, `network` and `resourceUrl` MUST be equal in the two, and `payer` and `transaction` (when the base receipt carries one) MUST name the same account and transaction.

requirements.text: Generate `receiptId` with at least 128 bits of secure randomness and never reuse one.
requirements.anchor: The issuer MUST generate at least 128 bits of it from a cryptographically secure source and MUST NOT reuse a value.

requirements.text: Use as `settlementRef` only a value the settlement result carried at the location §4.3 names; never compute one, and never take one from anywhere else.
requirements.anchor: An issuer MUST NOT use as `settlementRef` a value the settlement result did not carry, and MUST NOT compute one.

requirements.text: The settlement reference of `batch-settlement` on `solana:*` is `SettlementResponse.extra.commitmentId`; the receipt carries it beside the response's transaction, or with an empty one.
requirements.anchor: | `batch-settlement` on `solana:*` | `SettlementResponse.extra.commitmentId` |

requirements.text: Find the settlement reference by the table alone, from `accepted.scheme` and `accepted.network`: the scheme exactly, the namespace exactly; no row, no reference.
requirements.anchor: is found by this table and nothing else: take `accepted.scheme` and `accepted.network`

requirements.text: `chargedAmount` is `extra.chargedAmount` when present, failing that `amount` when present, failing that `""`; the lookup does not depend on the scheme.
requirements.anchor: It is `SettlementResponse.extra.chargedAmount` when present (§4.6); failing that `SettlementResponse.amount` when present; failing that `""`.

requirements.text: Never compute `chargedAmount`, for example from `accepted.amount`: with no charged amount in the response it is `""`.
requirements.anchor: The issuer MUST NOT compute `chargedAmount`, for example from `accepted.amount`.

requirements.text: Without a response payer, the payer is `authorization.from` when present, on any network, and `""` when neither has one.
requirements.anchor: none, it is `PaymentPayload.payload.authorization.from`, on any network, when present

requirements.text: May issue a later receipt for the same settlement, with `supersedes` set.
requirements.anchor: **`supersedes`.** A server MAY issue a later receipt for the same settlement when the payment's state changes or it corrects an earlier statement.

requirements.text: Carry a reversal or refund transaction in the reversal binding.
requirements.anchor: the server SHOULD carry it in the `action-receipt:reversal-transaction` binding

requirements.text: Hash only accepted requirements that lie in the value domain.
requirements.anchor: `accepted` MUST lie in the value domain of §4.6.

requirements.text: Issue no receipt when the requirements digest cannot be computed.
requirements.anchor: MUST NOT issue a receipt for that payment

requirements.text: Check that `accepted` is what the server offered before signing.
requirements.anchor: so the issuer checks that before it signs (§6.2 step 4)

requirements.text: A binding does not restate or contradict a core member.
requirements.anchor: An issuer SHOULD NOT carry a binding that restates or contradicts one

requirements.text: Read every x402 string as present or absent by the one definition of §4.6; an unpaired surrogate is absent, and the receipt built from that reading verifies.
requirements.anchor: The issuer and the verifier use this one definition, so they cannot disagree about whether a response carried a value.

requirements.text: An optional statement member that is missing or `null` is not given.
requirements.anchor: An optional statement member (`supersedes`, the reversal transaction, the further bindings) is not given when it is missing or `null`.

requirements.text: A given optional statement member is well formed, or the issuer refuses.
requirements.anchor: Given, it MUST be well formed (steps 8 and 10), and the issuer refuses if it is not.

requirements.text: x402 objects are read leniently: a value of the wrong type is absent.
requirements.anchor: **x402 objects are read leniently.**

requirements.text: Ignore unnamed members of the statement and of `action`, at those two levels only.
requirements.anchor: Members of the statement, and of its `action` object, that this section does not name are ignored.

requirements.text: A binding entry has exactly two members; one with another member is refused.
requirements.anchor: a binding entry has exactly two members (§4.5)

requirements.text: Treat the extension as advertised only when the entry is an object whose `info` is a JSON object.
requirements.anchor: The issuer **advertised** this extension when

requirements.text: The advertised `info` is read strictly: a member whose value is `null` is a member.
requirements.anchor: nothing in it is read leniently: a member of it whose value is `null` is a member, not an absence.

requirements.text: Perform the ten steps in order.
requirements.anchor: The issuer MUST perform these steps in order.

requirements.text: Issue nothing once a step fails.
requirements.anchor: At the first step that fails it MUST NOT issue a receipt.

requirements.text: Step 1: refuse unless settlement succeeded (strictly `true`).
requirements.anchor: `SettlementResponse.success` is `true`

requirements.text: Step 2: refuse without a transaction or a settlement reference.
requirements.anchor: the response has a `transaction`, or the issuer has a settlement reference (§4.3)

requirements.text: Step 3: refuse unless the accepted requirements are an object in the value domain.
requirements.anchor: `PaymentPayload.accepted` is a JSON object in the value domain of §4.6

requirements.text: Step 4: refuse unless `accepts` is an array and `accepted` equals one of its entries.
requirements.anchor: `PaymentRequired.accepts` is an array, and `accepted` equals one of its entries (below)

requirements.text: Compare `accepted` with each offered entry by JCS bytes, both in the value domain: equal by value is equal; a case difference is not.
requirements.anchor: `accepted` equals an entry of `accepts` when both are in the value domain and their JCS serializations are the same bytes.

requirements.text: Step 5: refuse unless the accepted network is a network identifier and does not conflict with a response network that is one.
requirements.anchor: `accepted.network` is a network identifier (§4.6); and, when `SettlementResponse.network` is also one, the two are equal

requirements.text: Step 6: refuse unless the resource URL is present; copy it verbatim.
requirements.anchor: `PaymentRequired.resource.url` is present

requirements.text: Step 7: refuse unless `payTo` is present and the identifiers satisfy the grammar after lowercasing.
requirements.anchor: `accepted.payTo` is present, and after the lowercasing below `payer`, `payTo` and `transaction` satisfy §4.6

requirements.text: Step 7: refuse when the charged amount found (§4.3) is outside the grammar of §4.6; never repair it.
requirements.anchor: and `chargedAmount` (§4.3) satisfies §4.6

requirements.text: The payload's `chargedAmount` is the value of §4.3, verbatim, or `""`.
requirements.anchor: `chargedAmount` is the value of §4.3, verbatim, or `""`

requirements.text: The payer is the response's when present, else `authorization.from` when present (on any network), else `""`.
requirements.anchor: `payer` is `SettlementResponse.payer` when present; failing that the scheme payload's payer when present

requirements.text: Lowercase `payer`, `payTo` and `transaction` on eip155 (ASCII only); copy them verbatim elsewhere.
requirements.anchor: When `accepted.network` begins `eip155:` the issuer lowercases `payer`, `payTo` and `transaction`

requirements.text: Never change the settlement reference, on any network.
requirements.anchor: The settlement reference is never changed.

requirements.text: Step 8: refuse a statement that is not well formed; each sub-check has its own exchange, with both sides of every bound.
requirements.anchor: **Well-formed statement (step 8).**

requirements.text: Step 9: refuse when an advertised `actionType` or `scope` is a member whose value is not a string equal to the statement's.
requirements.anchor: for each of `actionType` and `scope` that is a member of the advertised `info`, its value is a string equal to the statement's `action` member

requirements.text: Step 10: refuse bindings that break the shape, grammar, value form, uniqueness or count.
requirements.anchor: Two entries with one `type`, an entry that breaks the grammar of §4.5 or the value form of §4.5.2, or more than 16 entries fails the step.

requirements.text: Refuse a supplied binding in the `action-receipt:` namespace.
requirements.anchor: A further binding whose `type` begins `action-receipt:` fails the step

requirements.text: Add the advertisement binding when the extension was advertised.
requirements.anchor: if the issuer advertised this extension, add `action-receipt:advertised-info`

requirements.text: Refuse an advertised `info` outside the value domain.
requirements.anchor: An advertised `info` that is not in the value domain cannot be committed and fails the step

requirements.text: Add the reversal binding when the statement gives a reversal transaction, lowercased on eip155.
requirements.anchor: if the statement gives a reversal transaction, add `action-receipt:reversal-transaction` with that value, lowercased when `accepted.network` begins `eip155:`.

requirements.text: Emit bindings in ascending order of `type`.
requirements.anchor: Sort the entries in ascending order of `type`.

requirements.text: Build each member from the source the table names.
requirements.anchor: The Source column is normative for the issuer

requirements.text: Run §5.2 and §5.3 on the built payload and refuse if either fails (answer `self_check_failed`).
requirements.anchor: An implementation SHOULD nevertheless run those two checks on the payload it built and refuse if either fails
requirements.note: issuer.py runs a self-check suite that breaks eight members of an issued payload and requires self_check() to refuse each; flip_issuer.py disables the self-check and requires that suite to go red

requirements.text: Sign the JCS payload under a header that is the JCS serialization of the three members of §3.
requirements.anchor: header that is the JCS serialization of the three members of §3. It MUST:
requirements.note: issuer.py signs every issued exchange's payload with sign() and verifies it through both verifiers; flip_issuer.py replaces the JCS header by json.dumps and requires the suite to go red

requirements.text: Sign only under a `kid` the issuer's own source lists for `resourceUrl`, with a key of the type `alg` names.
requirements.anchor: use a key whose `kid` its own authorization source lists for `resourceUrl` (§5.4), and whose type matches `alg`
requirements.note: issuer.py's signing suite requires sign() to refuse an unlisted kid, a resource its source does not list, and three key/alg mismatches

requirements.text: Emit 64-byte `r || s` ECDSA signatures with low `s`, normalizing the library's output.
requirements.anchor: for `ES256` and `ES256K`, emit the 64-byte `r || s` form with `s <= n/2`, replacing `s` by `n - s` when the library returns the high form
requirements.note: issuer.py signs 400 payloads per algorithm with the library's randomized ECDSA and requires both verifiers to pass all of them, and an un-normalized control to be rejected at least once

requirements.text: Emit a compact string within the bound of §3.
requirements.anchor: emit a compact string within the bound of §3
requirements.note: issuer.py's signing suite requires sign() to refuse a payload whose compact string would exceed 65536

requirements.text: Every issued receipt, signed as §6.3 says, passes both verifiers in the context of its own exchange with the report §6.3 promises.
requirements.anchor: That verifier returns `PASS` with requirements `matched`, `payTo` `compared`, and, if the issuer advertised, `checks.advertisement` `matched`.
requirements.note: issuer.py signs every issued payload and compares both verifiers' reports with the §6.3 promise; fuzz_issuer.py property Q3 does the same for every generated exchange

requirements.text: Sign only after settlement returns.
requirements.anchor: Sign only after settlement returns.

requirements.text: Keep every signing key resolvable and never rebind a `kid`.
requirements.anchor: Keep every key that has signed a receipt resolvable for as long as receipts signed by it may need to be verified, and never rebind a `kid` to a different key

requirements.text: Use a signing key separate from the `payTo` key.
requirements.anchor: A dedicated signing key separate from the `payTo` key is RECOMMENDED

requirements.text: A later receipt for the same settlement follows §4.3.
requirements.anchor: A later receipt for the same settlement follows §4.3: same settlement members, `supersedes` set, a permitted status pair.

requirements.text: When both receipts are emitted, keep them consistent.
requirements.anchor: When both receipts are emitted, keep them consistent (§2.4).

requirements.text: Use pseudonymous `agent` and `scope` where possible.
requirements.anchor: `agent` and `scope` SHOULD be pseudonymous where the use case allows.

requirements.text: Issuer adapter protocol: answer every line, including lines a naive parser cannot read (any nesting depth, integers of any length) and lines that are not JSON (`invalid_input`); never report the issuer's own fault as a refusal.
requirements.anchor: An issuer conforms if, for every exchange under `exchanges/`, it produces exactly the expected payload or refuses with the expected reason
requirements.note: run_exchanges.py sends ten protocol cases (200000-deep nesting, 5000-digit integers, NaN, truncated and malformed deep lines), opaque ids, a shuffled order and a follow-up per exchange to every adapter

requirements.text: Read `settlementStatus`; a passing receipt does not mean 'paid'.
requirements.anchor: A verifier or consumer MUST NOT read a passing receipt as "paid": it MUST read `settlementStatus`.

requirements.text: Do not read payment status as delivery evidence, or outcome as payment evidence.
requirements.anchor: It MUST NOT read `settlementStatus` as evidence about delivery

requirements.text: Do not treat a binding that was not evaluated, or mismatched, as verified.
requirements.anchor: A consumer MUST NOT treat a `not_evaluated` or `mismatched` binding as verified.

requirements.text: Do not treat an unresolved key as a finding against the signer.
requirements.anchor: A consumer MUST NOT treat it as a finding against the signer.

requirements.text: Do not read PASS as covering what the report marks not compared or not evaluated.
requirements.anchor: A consumer MUST NOT read `PASS` as covering anything the report marks

requirements.text: Do not use a client-chosen identifier as the sole link between receipt and settlement.
requirements.anchor: MUST NOT be used as the sole link between a receipt and a settlement

requirements.text: Do not rely on a receipt for the current state of a payment; resolve the settlement on the rail.
requirements.anchor: A consumer that needs the current state of a payment MUST NOT rely on a receipt for it and resolves the settlement on the rail (§5.14).

requirements.text: Never count payments by `receiptRef` or `receiptId`.
requirements.anchor: A consumer MUST NOT count payments by `receiptRef` or `receiptId`.

requirements.text: Treat B as superseding A only when both pass, B names A's receiptRef, the settlement members are equal and the status pair is permitted; otherwise treat them as unrelated.
requirements.anchor: A consumer holding receipts `A` and `B` MUST treat `B` as superseding `A` only if all of these hold, and otherwise MUST treat the two as unrelated:

requirements.text: Do not pick one of two receipts that each validly supersede the same receipt.
requirements.anchor: Two receipts that each validly supersede the same receipt show that the signer issued inconsistent statements; a consumer MUST NOT pick one.

requirements.text: Never let a binding change how a member of §4.1 is read.
requirements.anchor: a consumer MUST NOT let a binding change how it reads a member of §4.1.

requirements.text: Do not read a signature failure on an old receipt as forgery unless the resolved key is known to be the one bound at issuedAt.
requirements.anchor: A consumer SHOULD NOT read a signature failure on an old receipt as proof the presenter forged it unless it knows the key it resolved is the key that was bound at `issuedAt`.

requirements.text: Do not treat a settlement-mismatch rejection of a receipt with a non-empty `settlementRef` as a finding against the signer unless the verifier held `accepted`.
requirements.anchor: a consumer MUST NOT treat a `invalid_actionreceipt_settlement_mismatch` on a non-empty `settlementRef` as a finding against the signer unless the verifier held `accepted`.

requirements.text: A requesting verifier supplies the URL it paid for.
requirements.anchor: MUST supply the URL it paid for
